title: How AI Agents Let GTM Teams Scale — Justin Joyce, Cloudflare

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Cloudflare OS is live, has vetted workflows, and the speaker discusses scaling, feedback loops, and what to tackle next after a 2x efficiency gain.

summary:
Joyce completes the Cloudflare OS picture by showing how the agentic workspace combines curated skill repositories, MCP data connections, and an AI gateway so reps can pull data and execute expert-level tasks during live customer work, including account planning, renewal preparation, upsell analysis, daily prescriptive planning, and on-the-fly QBR slide deck generation. A central alias routes skills through go-to-market and operations review so skills do not proliferate unchecked, and expert-level knowledge skills exist at every level of the business.

He then ties the three pillars together, arguing that without self-service, pushed insights, and scaled analysis, go-to-market needs go unmet. Skill curation is the foundation of the agentic workforce, embedding business knowledge into skill files used both by analysts and by reps inside Cloudflare OS, which makes outcomes more predictable and deterministic. A tight feedback loop, modeled like an external product launch, validates usefulness and efficiency, and layering the pillars lets the team serve requests, push information, and enable self-service through a single agentic stack. Joyce credits this combination with roughly 2x efficiency.

Looking forward, he flags deeper systems integration so QBR decks, renewal call skills, meeting notes, and embedded meeting artifacts work without manual pulls; harder problems around quoting, approvals, and Salesforce CRM writes that he plans to handle with the same kind of automated workflows and review he applied to analysis; and a Cambrian explosion of agents that will need a strategic, standardized approach so source-of-truth systems stay aligned.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and route into sales ops via machine learning
sections.summary: Joyce opens with humor about AGI pills, introduces himself as principal sales operations and strategy manager at Cloudflare working with revenue ops on lead generation and customer experience, and recounts spending seven years on the machine learning side at Grainger before returning to sales ops six months ago to apply those skills.

sections.title: Why traditional go to market does not scale
sections.summary: He argues back-office teams either rebuild weekly analyses in spreadsheets for hours at a time or ship dashboards that meet most needs but not all, leaving gaps in what go-to-market teams actually receive.

sections.title: The context gap and the expert gap
sections.summary: He defines the context gap, where reps must gather fresh information each time they switch between prospect, adoption, and customer satisfaction calls, and the expert gap between top reps and those still ramping, both of which create organizational inefficiency.

sections.title: Three pillars
sections.summary: He frames a three-pillar approach: scale analysis with business context so operations can shift toward strategy, scale insight by delivering the data's story to teams at the weekly level, and provide self-service expert capabilities to reps during customer conversations.

sections.title: Skill files that let non-SQL users query the data
sections.summary: He describes role-specific skill files carrying business context, schema knowledge, and tested question types such as closed-date and amount changes on opportunities, which let non-SQL users ask questions directly and turn two-hour tasks into five-minute ones. The same files let the team build internal applications without IT bottlenecks, freeing operations for strategy and enablement.

sections.title: There is a story in the data; stop making them search
sections.summary: He shows a synthetic weekly summary with trends, standouts, and watches, and argues insight should be pushed to teams because dashboard adoption is uneven. He explains pre-shaping data along time, logical dimensions like manager and theater, and metric, with filtering and aggregation logic embedded up front to handle about 80 percent of requests.

sections.title: Drafter reviewer tone agent workflow
sections.summary: He describes a multi-agent workflow with drafter, reviewer, and tone agents, plus observability on each LLM call, that the team read run-by-run for two to three months before trusting. He plans to extend it beyond leadership summaries down to the customer level.

sections.title: Cloudflare OS self-service agentic workspace
sections.summary: He introduces Cloudflare OS, an internal agentic workspace on Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects that gives reps per-user compute and persistent storage, with use cases already including forecast briefs and QBR decks, before trailing off into a purchase deck example.

sections.title: Cloudflare OS skill repository and use cases
sections.summary: He expands on Cloudflare OS use cases including onboarding customers, account planning, renewal preparation, and upsell analysis, and shows how the workspace combines curated expert skills, MCP connections, and an AI gateway so reps pull data and execute expert-level work during live customer situations. A central skill alias, curated by go-to-market and operations, prevents proliferation, and expert-level knowledge skills exist at every level. Screenshots show reps building a prescriptive daily plan and generating a custom QBR slide deck for a customer call.

sections.title: Recap of the three pillars
sections.summary: He ties the three pillars together, arguing that without self-service, pushed insights, and scaled analysis, go-to-market needs go unmet and opportunity cost rises when the analytical team is overloaded.

sections.title: Findings: curation, feedback, layering
sections.summary: He shares findings: skill curation embedding business knowledge into skill files for analysts and reps is the foundation for predictable, deterministic agentic outcomes; a tight internal feedback loop modeled on external product launches validates usefulness and efficiency; and layering the three pillars lets the team serve requests, push information, and enable self-service, collectively producing roughly 2x efficiency.

sections.title: Future work: systems integration, quoting, approvals, CRM, agent explosion
sections.summary: He outlines future work: deeper integration with systems so QBR decks, renewal skills, meeting notes, and embedded artifacts flow automatically, including security setup; harder problems around quoting, approvals, and Salesforce CRM writes, which he plans to handle with automated workflows and review similar to the analysis pipeline; and a Cambrian explosion of agents that requires a strategic, standardized approach so source-of-truth systems stay aligned across teams. He closes by thanking the audience.
